title: Intel Gives Upbeat Sales Forecast After PC Demand Picks Up
content:
Intel Corp. gave a stronger-than-anticipated revenue forecast for the current period, offering investors a glimmer of hope as they wait for a turnaround under new Chief Executive Officer Lip-Bu Tan.
Third-quarter sales will be $12.6 billion to $13.6 billion, the company said in a statement Thursday. Analysts on average had projected a number at the low end of that range.
Intel is benefiting from a resurgence in the personal-computer industry, driven in part by manufacturers’ efforts to build up inventory before tariffs hit. But the Silicon Valley pioneer still faces a variety of challenges. It has lost market share to rivals and is struggling to attract customers to its foundry business, which makes chips for outside clients. It also lacks products that can satisfy the massive demand for AI systems.
Senior Analyst Jay Goldberg of Seaport Research Partners says he believes the company doesn't have a coherent AI strategy. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Canada Retail Sales Bounced Back in June to End Weak Quarter
content: Canadian retail sales grew at the fastest pace this year in June, according to an official estimate, bouncing back from a slowdown in May.

title: Ukraine Keeps Rates on Hold as Government Seeks More IMF Aid
content: Ukraine’s central bank held its benchmark interest rate steady as the government prepares for new loan talks with the International Monetary Fund, with recent moves against anti-corruption agencies fueling donor concerns.

title: South Korea Weighs US Investment Pledge to Trim Auto Tariff
content: The US and South Korea have discussed creating a fund to invest in American projects as part of a trade deal, similar to an agreement Japan struck Tuesday with President Donald Trump, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Lagarde Says ECB in ‘Wait-and-See’ Mode After Holding Rates
content: President Christine Lagarde said the European Central Bank is in a “wait-and-see” mode after leaving interest rates unchanged for the first time in more than a year amid the US trade uncertainty.

title: Mexico’s Annual Inflation Slows, Paving Way for New Interest Rate Cut
content: Mexico’s annual inflation slowed more than expected in early July, supporting the central bank’s decision to leave the door open to further easing after last month’s interest rate cut.

title: Turkey Surprises With Bigger Than Expected Rate Cut to 43%
content: Turkey cut interest rates for the first time since March, when the arrest of a leading opposition figure halted the central bank’s recently adopted easing cycle.

title: US Jobless Claims Fall for a Sixth Week, Lowest Since Mid-April
content: Applications for US unemployment benefits fell for a sixth straight week, underscoring the resilience of the labor market.

title: Serbia Will Hoard All Its Gold at Home, Shunning Global Hubs
content: Serbia’s central bank plans to bring all of its roughly $6 billion-worth of gold reserves onto its own soil to ensure the security of the hoard in periods of crisis.

title: SpaceX’s Starlink Says Network Restored After Outage
content: SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service network has been restored after an hours-long outage, the Elon Musk-led unit said in a post on X.

title: Skydance’s Merger With Paramount Global Wins FCC’s Approval
content: Paramount Global’s merger with Skydance Media was approved by the US Federal Communications Commission, which backed the deal after the Trump administration extracted concessions on the news and entertainment company’s political coverage and diversity practices.

title: Citi Trading Desk Head Forced to Delete Post on Gaza Starvation
content: Citigroup Inc. pushed a trading desk head to delete a social-media post that was critical of Israel’s actions in Gaza and drew attention to widespread starvation in the region.

title: Liverpool FC CEO Says Player Spree Should Quell Ownership Gossip
content: Liverpool Football Club owner Fenway Sports Group remains committed to the team long term, the club’s Chief Executive Officer Billy Hogan said, adding that its multi-million pound spending spree over the summer should put speculation about its future ownership to bed.

title: Southwest’s CEO Sees Boeing Max 7 Certification Sliding to 2026
content: Boeing Co.’s 737 Max 7 jetliner won’t be certified until the first half of 2026, missing the US planemaker’s target of wrapping up work this year, according to the model’s largest customer.

title: Puma Slashes Outlook as New CEO Confronts Weak Demand, Tariffs
content: Puma SE slashed its earnings forecast for the year amid strikingly weak demand for its sports and athleisure products and growing concerns about the potential impacts of US tariffs.

title: Chevron’s Return to Venezuela Set to Boost US Refiners’ Supplies
content: The US government’s decision to let Chevron Corp. resume producing and exporting Venezuelan oil is set to increase crude supplies for American refiners by more than 200,000 barrels a day. Still, it may be too late for fuelmakers to take full advantage of the boost during the key summer driving season.

title: Australia’s Wheat Outlook Shows Little Improvement Despite Rain
content: Australia remains on track for a smaller wheat crop this season despite better rainfall in key growing regions, a blow to buyers such as China which may need more imports following a lengthy drought.

title: FAA Sees No Link to Mechanical Issue in Air India Boeing Crash
content: The new leader of the US Federal Aviation Administration said the deadly crash of an Air India Boeing Co. 787 jet last month was unlikely to have been caused by a mechanical issue with the plane or inadvertent movement of the aircraft’s fuel control switches.

title: Southwest Falls on $1 Billion Profit Cut From Tariff Fallout
content: Southwest Airlines Co. plunged after the carrier said it expects economic turmoil to wipe out as much as $1 billion of its annual pre-tax profit this year and offered shareholders a much-reduced outlook for the balance of 2025.

title: Darling Slumps Even as Trump’s Biofuel Policy Seen Aiding Profit
content: Darling Ingredients Inc. said US renewable fuel policies are shaping up to boost profits, yet investors focused on lingering uncertainties sent the company’s shares down the most since 2022.

title: FCC Chair ‘Pleased’ With Skydance-Paramount Deal Concessions
content: Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr said he’s happy with some of the concessions Skydance Media said it’s willing to make to win approval for its takeover of Paramount Global.

title: Krispy Kreme Owner Takes Offices at Fifth Avenue Skyscraper
content: JAB Holding Co., the investment firm behind Krispy Kreme Inc., signed a lease at a new 1,002-foot-tall tower on Manhattan’s Fifth Avenue.

title: Tesla’s Business Isn’t Better Off Than It Was Years Ago

title: Tesla Has a Problem — and It’s Not Just the Elon Musk Backlash
content: Tesla Inc. is in a sales slump, with deliveries of its electric vehicles on track to decline for the second full year in a row. Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk has warned that there could be “a few rough quarters” ahead for the company amid the loss of purchase incentives in the US.

title: Iberdrola’s Share Sale Draws €19 Billion in Investor Orders
content: Iberdrola SA’s capital increase attracted orders for about 3.8-times the stock available, suggesting robust appetite for European stock sales.

title: Sarepta Shares Drop After FDA Asks for More Data on Elevidys
content: The Food and Drug Administration won’t sign off on Sarepta Therapeutics Inc. bringing its controversial gene therapy back to the market until the company can persuade US regulators that it won’t cause more deaths, according to an official familiar with the situation.

title: American Air Falls on Raising Doubts About US Travel Rebound
content: American Airlines Group Inc. scaled back its earnings outlook amid deep fare discounts offered to woo reluctant travelers back on flights during a slump in consumer demand, sending its shares tumbling.

title: Prosecutor Who Tried Jan. 6 Cases Speaks Out About His Dismissal
content: Michael Gordon’s name never made headlines, but the cases he handled did. As a federal prosecutor in Tampa, Florida, he went after fentanyl dealers, armed robbers, and drug crews. When the Justice Department asked for volunteers to help prosecute people who attacked the US Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021, he raised his hand.

title: Union Pacific Nears Norfolk Deal to Create $200 Billion Railroad
content: Union Pacific Corp., North America’s largest railroad, is in advanced discussions with Norfolk Southern Corp. about a potential tie-up in what would be the industry’s largest deal ever.

title: EON Seen Raising Investments by €11 Billion Through 2030
content: German power utility EON SE is likely to increase spending by about €11 billion ($12.9 billion) by the end of the decade as the country makes grid investments more attractive, according to a report from Bernstein.

title: Permira, Nordic in Takeover Talks for Vaccine Maker Bavarian
content: A consortium consisting of Nordic Capital and Permira is in talks for a potential takeover of Bavarian Nordic A/S, a Copenhagen-listed vaccine maker.

title: Arabica Coffee Advances as Weather Risks Add to Supply Concerns
content: Arabica coffee rose for a third day, its longest winning streak in more than two months, amid worries over crop yields in Brazil and potential tariffs.

title: Deutsche Bank Hits Decade High as Sewing’s Strategy Pays Off
content: Deutsche Bank AG’s shares rose to the highest in a decade after reporting better-than-expected trading results, as Germany’s largest bank continues its recovery under Chief Executive Officer Christian Sewing.

title: Blackstone Profit Jumps 25% on Retail, Evergreen Fees
content: Blackstone Inc. reported a 25% jump in distributable earnings for the second quarter, buoyed by profits from its retail and evergreen funds.
